name: What kind of maintenance or follow-up should I expect after a major remodel or new addition is finished?

mainEntity.name: What kind of maintenance or follow-up should I expect after a major remodel or new addition is finished?

acceptedAnswer.text:
After a major remodel or addition, expect a short adjustment period where minor issues—like sticking doors, small paint touch-ups, or caulking cracks—may appear as the home settles. A good contractor anticipates this and includes a warranty and punch-list process.

You’ll also need to maintain new systems and finishes according to manufacturer guidelines to protect warranties. Some items, like sealants or grout, may need periodic inspection.

Key factors:
- Warranty length and what it covers (labor vs. materials)
- Scheduled follow-up visit or defined punch-list period
- Maintenance requirements for roofing, caulking, grout, and finishes
- Documentation of appliances, fixtures, and systems installed

Before final payment, confirm the warranty terms, get all manuals and paint codes, and schedule any agreed follow-up visits. Keeping a simple maintenance log and photo record of your project will make any future repairs or upgrades easier to manage.
